title: Residential edge — the taped line above Station Twelve

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Third time I've asked. Who signed the closure on Cluster B? A name, not a department.

nodes.speaker: noor
nodes.text: And third time I've answered. You're standing inside a taped line I didn't tape.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: You came through the north mouth on your own. That gate's rated for two. So who lifted the other half?

nodes.speaker: mara
nodes.text: It lifts for one. Slowly.

nodes.speaker: noor
nodes.text: Venn. You're on my sheet for eleven, and it's twenty past.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Dax Ren. I print the Quay Ledger — four pages and a photocopier. Cluster B, night of the surge: two of three pumps off at 02:31. Whose order?

nodes.speaker: mara
nodes.text: Mara Venn. I'm here for a pump.

nodes.speaker: noor
nodes.text: Nobody's order. The permit on this site says recovery contractor, three crew, daylight hours. Visitors clear through the borough office on Kell Street, which is shut, which is why nobody—

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: —hear that? Third time it's done that since I got here. Write down what it was and I'll wait.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: —which is why nobody has to answer anything. Kell Street. Give me the name of one person who is at Kell Street.

nodes.speaker: renna
nodes.text: Noor. Guide vane's fouled on twelve and my torch is under two feet of water.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: You were down there on the night. Were you on shift at half past two?

nodes.speaker: renna
nodes.text: I was on the pumps. I'm not on your paper.

nodes.speaker: renna
nodes.text: They didn't trip, though. I've heard them trip. These eased off, one after another, ten seconds apart. Like somebody turning a tap down.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Ten seconds apart is a sequence, that isn't weather, somebody typed that, so who was on the desk, was it the optimizer or was it a person, because the report says overcurrent and overcurrent doesn't count to ten—

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: —sorry. That was five questions. I do that.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: That's the gate. Fine. Slower.

nodes.speaker: mara
nodes.text: Ten seconds is a ramp. Not a breaker.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: You're carrying a paper set with wet corners. Holt doesn't ask for paper when the tablet's right. Does the valve schedule match?

choices.text: Keep her name out of it and I'll walk you to the gate.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Doesn't match. Good. I'll print "a municipal technician on site" and you'll hate that, and it'll still be true.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: "Whoever updated it." Not "they match." Not "the tablet's fine." You've been inside the seal ten minutes and you already sound like the office.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Her name for a walk to a gate I got over on my own. Fine. Keep her. I'll take the ten seconds.

nodes.speaker: noor
nodes.text: Take what you like. Mine's the name on the site form — twelve years of licence, and my daughter sits her tickets in spring on my references. That's what the tape is.

nodes.speaker: renna
nodes.text: I'm taking the spare torch. And Noor — something's living in the crew van. It's been at your seat.

nodes.speaker: mara
nodes.text: Stand off the plate. I'm pulsing the feeder.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Before you do. The borough report gives me 02:14, then it gives me 03:06. In between I have four dispatch calls with receipts and not one of them is on that page.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: So read what the log says the pump did at 02:47. Then tell me whether it matches what she just described—

nodes.speaker: noor
nodes.text: That's a survey pulse. Now we all stand here with a maintenance unit until somebody cancels it.

nodes.speaker: mara
nodes.text: It was me. It can stand.

nodes.speaker: dax
nodes.text: Aldis Row. The stairwell behind the laundrette, second landing, above the water. If that log says overcurrent, come and tell me so. If it doesn't — come faster.
